evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/util/url_validator.rs:150 — the Host::Ipv6 arm of validate_fetch_url() only rejects is_loopback(), fc00::/7 (unique-local) and fe80::/10 (link-local). It never normalizes IPv4-mapped / IPv4-compatible IPv6 addresses, so an attacker-supplied feed/import URL like https://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/latest/meta-data/ parses as Host::Ipv6, passes every check, and reaches the cloud metadata endpoint at fetch time. Ipv6Addr::is_loopback() is false for ::ffff:127.0.0.1, so ::ffff:10.0.0.5, ::ffff:127.0.0.1 and ::ffff:169.254.169.254 all bypass the carefully-written IPv4 private-range block above (url_validator.rs:96-146).

backend/servers/reality-server/src/util/url_validator.rs:71 — this validator is the documented SSRF gate for user-supplied server-side-fetched URLs (agency import feeds); the IPv4-mapped gap defeats its stated purpose. Fix: call ip.to_ipv4_mapped()/to_ipv4() and, when Some(v4), run the same IPv4 forbidden-range checks; also reject NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 and unspecified ::.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:147 — check_redirect_uri_allowed() treats any value that starts_with('/') && !starts_with("//") as a trusted same-origin relative path and returns Ok() unconditionally, skipping the allowlist. It only guards the literal protocol-relative form //evil.com.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:305 — the SSO callback feeds the stored redirect_uri straight into Redirect::temporary() (sso.rs:338). Browsers normalize backslashes to forward slashes in the authority, so a stored redirect_uri of /\evil.com or /\/evil.com passes the relative-path shortcut here yet the browser resolves the Location header as //evil.com -> protocol-relative navigation to attacker origin = open redirect out of the post-auth SSO flow (issue #820 class). Fix: reject any path containing a backslash before the relative-path shortcut, or parse with a trusted base and verify the resolved origin is same-origin.
